meta.title: Security
meta.description: How BIShare keeps your files private: end-to-end encryption with keys that never leave your devices, local transfers that never touch a server, and remote shares that delete themselves after 24 hours.

hero.title: Private by design
hero.sub: Your files travel sealed, take the shortest possible path, and leave nothing behind. Not because of a setting you found — because of how BIShare is built.

flowHeading: How an end-to-end encrypted transfer works

encryption.title: Locked before it leaves. Unlocked on arrival.
encryption.sub: Only the two devices in a transfer can read the files moving between them. Here is what happens under the hood — in plain words, with the technology named once.

handshake.title: A secret agreed in silence
handshake.desc: Before anything moves, both devices agree on a shared secret without ever sending it across the network. Someone recording every packet of that handshake still ends up with nothing usable.

perFile.title: Every file gets its own key
perFile.desc: Each transfer is sealed with a fresh key of its own. Even in the worst imaginable case, one key could only ever open one file — never your history, never the next transfer.

cipher.title: Sealed and tamper-evident
cipher.desc: Files are scrambled with the same cipher class that protects banking and government traffic — with a built-in seal. If a single byte is altered in transit, the transfer is rejected.

local.label: Local-first
local.title: Your network is the whole journey.
local.body: When two devices share the same Wi-Fi or hotspot, files travel straight between them. There is no upload step, no middleman, and no copy anywhere else — because there is no server in the path at all.
points: Nearby transfers never touch a server — not ours, not anyone's
Works completely offline: Wi-Fi or a phone hotspot is enough
Nothing stored in the cloud means nothing to leak from it
Files exist in exactly two places: the sender and the receiver

visual.srBeam: A file travels directly from your phone to your laptop over your own network.
visual.noServer: No server is contacted. The transfer starts and ends on your own network.

remote.label: Remote shares
remote.title: Protected in transit. Gone in 24 hours.
remote.body: When the other person is on a different network, your file takes a short, guarded detour through secure cloud storage. It is encrypted on the way there, encrypted while it waits, and deleted on schedule — every time.
points: Encrypted in transit and encrypted at rest
Deleted automatically after 24 hours — no action needed
One-time links self-destruct after the first download
We never scan, index, or look at what you share

transit.title: Encrypted in transit
transit.desc: Sealed on the way up and on the way down.

rest.title: Encrypted at rest
rest.desc: Stored scrambled while it waits to be picked up.

deleted.title: Deleted after 24 hours
deleted.desc: Automatically, whether or not it was downloaded.

dont.title: What we don't do
dont.sub: Privacy is mostly about restraint. These aren't settings you have to find — they're how BIShare works, by default and always.

tracking.title: No tracking
tracking.desc: No behavioral profiles, no advertising identifiers, no following you around the internet.

ads.title: No ads
ads.desc: BIShare is a tool, not an ad network. Your attention is not the product.

selling.title: No selling data
selling.desc: We don't sell, rent, or trade your data. There is no data broker on the other end.

scanning.title: No file scanning
scanning.desc: We never open, scan, or analyze what you transfer. Your files are your business.

disclosure.title: Found a weakness? Tell us first.
disclosure.body: Security claims are only as good as the scrutiny they survive. If you discover a vulnerability in BIShare, email us with the steps to reproduce it. We read every report, and good-faith research is always welcome.

flow.srDescription: Device A encrypts the file, the encrypted data travels across the network, and only Device B can decrypt it. The encryption keys never leave either device.

sealed.title: Sealed on your device
sealed.desc: The file is encrypted before a single byte leaves.

transit.title: Ciphertext in transit
transit.desc: The network only ever carries scrambled noise.

unlocked.title: Unlocked on arrival
unlocked.desc: Only the receiving device holds the matching key.
